 MULESH S/O SAWAL SINGH, AGED 21 YEARS,

AND  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH THROUGH POLICE  STATION JOBAT DISTRICT ALIRAJPUR (MADHYA  PRADESH)
 
 ( BY SHRI AJAY RAJ GUPTA - PANEL LAWYER)
 This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:
 ORDER

This is the third application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No. 158/2020 registered at Police Station Jobat District Alirajpur (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 363, 366, 376, 376(2)(N), 376(2)(F),
506, 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
The applicant is in custody since 3.5.2020.
2. As per prosecution story, on 29.4.2020 father of prosecutrix/complainant lodged a missing person report at police station Jobat about missing of her daughter from home.
Prosecutrix was recovered and it has been gathered that present applicant alongwith co-accused abducted the prosecutrix and took her in a forest and committed repeatedly rape upon her.
Accordingly, offence has been registered against the applicant.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is an innocent person and he has been falsely implicated in this offence.
He is in custody since 3.5.2020 (excluding period of 60 days on which applicant was granted temporary bail).

Other material witnesses have been examined Mulesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68522433/
1 before the trial court, therefore, there is no apprehension to tamper with the prosecution evidence.

sentences.text: The applicant is permanent resident of District Alirajpur.
Prosecutrix was major at the time of incident and was remained in the company of applicant with her own accord.
Final conclusion of the trial is likely to take sufficient long time.
Under the above circumstances, prayer for grant of bail may be considered on such terms and conditions, as this Court deems fit and proper.
4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / State opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection.

5. Perused the impugned order of the trial Court as well as the case diary.
6.

After considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, nature and gravity of offence,
arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant and also taking note of the fact that applicant has already suffered jail incarceration for about 2 years, prosecutrix is a major lady, most of material witnesses have been examined before the trial court but final conclusion of the trial will take sufficient long time.
In these circumstances, I deem it proper to release the applicant on bail.
Therefore, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

7. It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.75,000/- (Rupees Seventy Five Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court, as and when required.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) Cr.P.C.
Certified copy as per rules.

(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE BDJ Mulesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68522433/
